classification.difficultyReason: Construct a general proof by pairing tangent segments at all four vertices.

content.prompt:
The four sides of a quadrilateral are tangent to the same circle as shown below. Prove that
$$a+c=b+d.$$

spec.description: Unfilled circle tangent to all four sides of a quadrilateral, with a on the left, b above, c on the right and d below.
spec.mathematics: Vertices are intersections of tangents with unit-circle normal directions 25, 105, 180 and 270 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No split-segment variables or proof steps are supplied in the question diagram.

answer.short:
$a+c=b+d$.

Equal tangent pairs give $a=w+z$, $b=w+x$, $c=x+y$ and $d=y+z$, so both sums equal $w+x+y+z$.
answer.worked:
Let the equal tangent segments from the top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left vertices have lengths $w$, $x$, $y$ and $z$, respectively. Tangent segments from the same external point are equal, so
$$\begin{align*}a&=w+z\\b&=w+x\\c&=x+y\\d&=y+z.\end{align*}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}a+c&=(w+z)+(x+y)\\a+c&=(w+x)+(y+z)\\a+c&=b+d.\end{align*}$$
